source.title: Data Augmentation as Feature Manipulation: a story of desert cows and grass cows
source.authors: Ruoqi Shen; Sébastien Bubeck; Suriya Gunasekar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Theoretical and experimental results examine how augmentation changes generalization and overfitting in specified models, using different settings from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study tests data augmentation and view balance as conditions affecting train/test performance. Its main theory also analyzes memorization of dominant noise, but does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels. Figure-only experimental accuracy curves are not transcribed as precise numbers. Results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes augmentation and feature imbalance, without testing any specified version. Section 2.2 discusses random-label memorization capacity, but does not establish the paired training-recipe and held-out comparisons required by V1. Its linear versus nonlinear comparisons do not test V3's convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that augmentation changes features' relative contributions to learning, helping informative features compete with noise or spurious features. Their theory establishes this for a restricted nonlinear network, distribution, and stopping time; experiments provide broader supporting evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines data augmentation and view balance as feature manipulation, with a theoretical patch-wise network and CIFAR-10 and synthetic experiments; it does not reproduce the claim versions' stated protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Augmentation's effect depends on spurious-feature positions, spurious-feature fraction, noise magnitude, and the proportion of balanced examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Without augmentation, the theoretical network fits training data while failing on minor views; balancing views yields a vanishing test-error bound at the specified stopping time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Augmentation that balances feature views can promote rare-feature learning over noise memorization in the analyzed distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing spurious-feature positions improves accuracy in the separated-position settings. For positions (15,16), augmented accuracy is described as approximately stable across p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Position augmentation can weaken spurious-feature learning, with behavior depending on feature positions and prevalence.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed augmented variants improve accuracy over using their independent source images alone; at p ≥ 0.5, performance approaches that of the full independent dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fixed augmented variant can provide nearly the accuracy benefit of an additional independent image in this CIFAR-10 setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding dominant-view examples can leave balanced-test accuracy unchanged or lower at moderate noise, while helping at sufficiently high noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of additional dominant-view data depends on noise and view balance, even with convolutional architectures.

record.problems: The formal result is limited to a high-dimensional multi-view distribution, a two-layer patch-wise network with a special activation and logarithmic width, full-batch gradient descent, and a specified stopping time. Experimental comparisons are reported mainly in figures; exact values are not supplied in the text. The synthetic spurious-feature experiment uses CIFAR-10 cat and dog classes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figure-only curves were recorded qualitatively because exact values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Matched training on fixed random versus natural labels, with training fit and held-out accuracy for both. Section 2.2 supplies an informal capacity argument rather than this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects, including joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments that the augmentation findings are unreadable. The supplied text does not support the record's T2 classification or its absent-effect interpretation of R4.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fixed random-label and natural-label training with held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparison.
No large versus small batch comparison.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: two layer patch-wise convolutional network (3)
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent; evaluated at earliest constant-margin training time
rows.operation_detail: Train without data augmentation on the theoretical multi-view distribution with dominant noise.

conditions.value: distribution D; Assumption 2; minor views satisfy nρk ≤ o(σξ^q)
at first constant-margin training time T

rows.measure: test error lower bound on examples with minor views
rows.value: Pr[yF(w(t),x)<0] ≥ (1/2 − O(1/√C)) Σ(k=2 to K)ρk for all 0 ≤ t ≤ T
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − O(n²K³ log d / poly(d)) as stated in theorem proof
rows.note: The theorem states perfect training accuracy at T while minor views have not been learned; the test-error lower bound is a distributional result, not a random-label experiment.
rows.check: The theorem measures failure to learn rare features, not any specified version. Its stated success probability is 1 − O(n²K/poly(d)); Appendix E.2 uses n²K log d, not the record's n²K³ log d. The error bound is unconditional population error, weighted by minor-view frequencies, rather than error conditional on minor views.

rows.subject: two layer patch-wise convolutional network (3)
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent with data augmentation; evaluated at earliest constant-margin training time
rows.operation_detail: Train on the augmented distribution that balances all K feature views.

conditions.value: augmented dataset with equal representation of each feature view
at first constant-margin training time T aug

rows.baseline: without augmentation, test error lower bound in R1
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − O(n²K³ log d / poly(d)) as stated in theorem proof
rows.note: The result concerns the paper's theoretical distribution and assumptions.
rows.check: The augmentation theorem is correctly summarized but measures no specified version; its small test-error bound alone does not establish V1.

conditions.value: synthetic two-class dataset; balanced test set
SGD, momentum 0.9; weight decay 0.05; learning rate 0.1 annealed to 0.01 at epoch 100

rows.value: Dfull is consistently on par or lower when σξ is not too large; at very large σξ, Dbal can have low accuracy while Dfull learns the dominant view well; exact values figure only
